description:
FILED s465 (Fable, 2026-09-03) from the BA merge-review probe battery (scratchpad p1028/fh.pl row 7).  PRE-EXISTING, both emission paths.

    open(FH, '<', '/etc/passwd');
    print -e "FH";     # perl: "" -- a STRING operand is a PATH (no file ./FH); PCL: 1 -- it found the OPEN HANDLE named FH

perl's stat/filetest operand rule: a bareword (or a glob / IO ref) is a handle; a STRING is always a path -- `stat "STDIN"` stats a file called STDIN.  PCL's `%p-stat-arg` resolves a string that names an open handle to that handle, so a program that tests a file whose name coincides with a handle name gets the handle's answer.  Rare in practice, but silent and in the wrong direction (too permissive).  The `-t` filetest is the one that DOES accept a string handle name in perl?  -- probe before fixing: perlfunc says -t takes a filehandle; measure `-t "STDIN"` in perl 5.40.3 and keep whatever it does.
Fix: the string arm of `%p-stat-arg` is a path, full stop (the bareword arrives as a SYMBOL since #1032, so the string arm no longer needs the handle lookup).  Guard row in Pl/t/bareword-fh-slot-01.t.  Bars: cl/ change -> sweep + companion io/ + op/.
RELATED: #1032, the new task on missing operand kinds (glob value / glob ref / dirhandle / std streams).


=== DONE (s470bs) ===

SHIPPED in the resolver commit (runtime only).  The string arm of the operand
reading is a PATH, full stop â the handle lookup is gone from it.

THE `-t` QUESTION THE TASK ASKED TO PROBE FIRST WAS MEASURED, and the answer
is that `-t` IS the exception (perl 5.40.3):

    -t "STDIN"        ""     errno 25 (ENOTTY)   <- it FOUND the handle
    -t "/etc/passwd"  undef  errno  9 (EBADF)    <- no handle of that name

so `-t` keeps resolving a string as a handle NAME, and that is now written
down in `%p--t-handle`'s docstring as the one exception to the rule.  (`-t`
also gained the overload dispatch and the errno in the same pass.)

Guard row 28 of `Pl/t/bareword-fh-slot-01.t` (`-e "FH"` is 0 while FH is open)
and rows 56-57 (`-t`'s two errnos), inverse-verified against 027ba9c.
subject: SILENT WRONG (pre-existing, wrong direction): a STRING in a stat/filetest slot is a PATH in perl, but PCL resolves a string that names an OPEN handle to that handle -- `open(FH,...); -e "FH"` is "" in perl (no file ./FH) and 1 in PCL
